questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
The diagram shows a firm operating in monopolistic competition. At which point is the firm allocatively efficient? revenue MC AC / costs A B C MR AR O D output
The amount of training undertaken in a mixed economy is not socially optimal. What could explain this?

options.A: Experienced educators are a scarce resource.
options.B: In a mixed economy training is a public good.
options.C: The individual’s benefit from training is less than the benefit to society.
options.D: Training is a large variable cost for firms.

questions.questionText: Four bus companies control more than two-thirds of the market in a country. Critics claim that these companies fix prices on some routes to maximise revenue whilst lowering prices on other routes to stop smaller competitors entering the market. Which anti-competitive practices are these companies accused of?

options.A: collusion and limit pricing
options.B: collusion and price leadership
options.C: limit pricing and price discrimination
options.D: price leadership and x-inefficiency

questions.questionText: On a diagram the slope of a consumer’s budget line becomes steeper. What can definitely be concluded from this?

options.A: The consumer’s income has fallen.
options.B: The consumer’s income has risen.
options.C: The price has decreased for the product on the horizontal axis.
options.D: The price has increased for the product on the horizontal axis.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows two indifference curves and two budget lines for goods X and Y. good Y Y H F G IC IC O X X
The table shows the total costs at different levels of output for a firm producing chairs. output total cost (chairs) ($) 0 50
At which level of output will a firm achieve the aim of sales maximisation?

options.A: where AC = AR
options.B: where AC = MC
options.C: where MC = AR
options.D: where MR = zero

questions.questionText: In market economies firms can operate under monopolistic competition. Which feature is not typical of this type of market?

options.A: non-price competition through advertising
options.B: price leadership with few large firms
options.C: promotion of differentiated products
options.D: unrestricted entry results in long-run normal profit

questions.questionText: When will the ‘principal-agent’ problem occur?

options.A: when managers are not allowed to become shareholders
options.B: when members of a cartel collude to gain higher profit
options.C: when one firm dominates the market
options.D: when owners have different objectives to managers

questions.questionText: Which feature of oligopoly is being assumed when the demand curve for an individual firm is as shown? price D D O quantity

options.A: price discrimination
options.B: price leadership by the dominant firm
options.C: interdependence between firms
options.D: collusion between firms

questions.questionText: The table provides data on the number and value of mergers in Europe and North America between 2014 and 2017. Europe North America year number value (euro) number value (US dollar) 2014 17000 980 billion 14000 2289 billion 2015 15500 1161 billion 14500 2533 billion 2016 18100 1003 billion 15100 1858 billion 2017 18000 980 billion 18500 1822 billion What can be deduced from the table?

options.A: The average value of a merger in Europe was higher in 2017 than 2014.
options.B: The difference in the number of mergers in Europe and North America was the same in 2014 and 2016.
options.C: The value of mergers each year in US dollars was always lower in Europe.
options.D: The number of mergers each year was always higher in Europe.

questions.questionText: Charities distribute plastic bags to households that householders can fill with clothes they no longer want. The charities then collect them and sell the clothes to raise funds. Only one charity leaves a note thanking the householder for the donation. What best describes this charity’s approach?

options.A: game theory
options.B: monopoly behaviour
options.C: non-price competition
options.D: nudge theory

questions.questionText: What could prevent a market failure?

options.A: barriers to entry
options.B: building regulations
options.C: growth of firms
options.D: persuasive advertising

questions.questionText: When will a society have achieved an equitable distribution of income?

options.A: when all individuals have equal job opportunities
options.B: when all workers are paid the same wages
options.C: when the incomes within the society are equally distributed
options.D: when the society believes that the distribution of income is fair

questions.questionText: ‘The addition to revenue which results from employing one additional unit of a factor of production, while the quantities of all other factors of production remain constant’. What does this define?

options.A: marginal factor cost
options.B: marginal revenue
options.C: marginal revenue product
options.D: the law of diminishing returns

questions.questionText: The alternative to work is to have leisure time. The diagram shows a worker’s decision of how many hours of labour to supply. Z real wage rate supply of labour Y X O hours of labour What happens between Y and Z?

options.A: Extra leisure is preferred to work.
options.B: Extra work is preferred to leisure.
options.C: The job now requires more specific skills.
options.D: The price elasticity of supply for the final product has become more inelastic.

questions.questionText: By moving from rural areas to large urban areas to work, how might economic migrants create benefits in both areas in developing countries? rural areas urban areas

options.A: by improving land ownership systems by becoming better educated
options.B: by receiving financial help from urban workers by providing necessary labour
options.C: by reducing population pressure on resources by living in informal settlements
options.D: by solving unemployment problems by obtaining loans from moneylenders

questions.questionText: Which change is most likely to increase both economic growth and economic development in the long run?

options.A: a decrease in the saving ratio
options.B: an increase in investment in human capital
options.C: the depletion of non-renewable resources
options.D: the greater use of compulsory overtime working of labour

questions.questionText: The table gives population data from the United Nations. low-income lower-middle- upper-middle- high-income countries income countries income countries countries rate of population 2.7 1.5 0.8 0.5 change (% per year) life expectancy 61 67 74 80 (years) death rate (per 1000

The diagram shows selected US labour statistics from 2001 to 2013. 300 65 net new jobs 200 64 employed as a monthly average percentage of 100 63 (thousands) population aged 0 62 16 and over –100 61 –200 60 –300 59 –400 58 –500 2001 03 05 07 09 11 2013 year What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Between 2004 and 2005, when the number of net new jobs was rising, the percentage employed increased.
options.B: Employed as a percentage of the population aged 16 and over declined continuously.
options.C: The natural rate of unemployment was achieved only in 2008.
options.D: The number of employed workers rose in all except four years.

questions.questionText: What indicates that a developing country is becoming less dependent on foreign aid?

options.A: It gains foreign currency by exporting a range of raw materials, and uses this to import machinery from developed economies.
options.B: It has to change its economic structure in order to qualify for a bailout loan from the World Bank.
options.C: Its balance of payments goes into deficit when it has to start paying interest on loans taken out with foreign banks.
options.D: Its local firms go out of business after a foreign multinational sets up in the country.

questions.questionText: How must GDP at market prices (producer prices) be adjusted to find GDP at factor cost?

options.A: by adding exports and deducting imports
options.B: by adding net property income and deducting transfer payments
options.C: by adding profits and deducting income taxes
options.D: by adding subsidies and deducting indirect taxes

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the equilibrium levels of national income in a closed economy with no government, at two levels of investment, I and I .
An upward shift of the curve relating consumption to national income could be caused by

options.A: a reduction in taxation.
options.B: an increase in investment.
options.C: an increase in national income.
options.D: an increase in savings.

questions.questionText: Which combination of changes is most likely to result in an increase in the demand for money? income price interest level level rate

options.A: fall fall rise
options.B: fall rise fall
options.C: rise fall rise
options.D: rise rise fall

questions.questionText: In 1936 Keynes explained how economic policy can be used to increase aggregate demand and prevent an economic depression. Which policy supports Keynes’ theory?

options.A: Central banks should raise interest rates and decrease liquidity.
options.B: Governments should increase expenditure and decrease taxation.
options.C: Governments should encourage consumer savings rather than expenditure.
options.D: Trading policy should prevent the free movement of capital.

questions.questionText: A central bank increases the money supply in an attempt to stimulate investment and growth when the economy is in recession. When might this policy be ineffective?

options.A: if the economy is in the liquidity trap
options.B: if the economy is in the poverty trap
options.C: if the Marshall-Lerner condition does not hold
options.D: if the value of the multiplier is very low

questions.questionText: Which statement describes what the Phillips curve shows?

options.A: An inverse relationship exists between inflation and unemployment.
options.B: As employment increases the balance of payments deteriorates.
options.C: Economic growth and employment have a positive relationship.
options.D: It is possible to achieve low inflation and high economic growth at the same time.

questions.questionText: To stimulate economic growth the government increases the size of its budget deficit and funds this by increasing the money supply. What is most likely to reduce the effectiveness of these measures in achieving their aim?

options.A: a floating exchange rate
options.B: a high marginal propensity to import
options.C: a low marginal propensity to save
